result.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
result.summary: The performance of an LLM agent depends on both its model and its harness, the code that mediates its interaction with tools and environments. Can LLM researchers drive this co-evolution as a recursive improvement process, deciding round after round which component to change when each change alters the value of the other? Existing benchmarks evaluate post-training or data research with the harness out of scope, or harness optimization with the model fixed, leaving this joint decision unmeasured. We introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs as researchers co-evolving the model and harness of a target agent across five agentic domains. Researchers start from a common base model and initial harness, train and revise within a 24-hour budget, and submit a model-harness pair that is scored on separate test tasks. Across five frontier researchers, the strongest closes more than four fifths of the gap to an instruction-tuned reference system, and co-evolution succeeds on interaction tasks but rarely on long-horizon coding. These results suggest that current LLMs can make a strong first improvement, but cannot yet turn feedback from an improved system into the next one. CoEvoBench provides a controlled testbed for measuring the research capabilities that recursive co-evolution requires.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoEvoBench：让 LLM 充当研究者，在 24 小时预算内联合改进目标 agent 的模型与 harness，并在独立测试任务上评分以考察五个 agentic 领域的递归协同演化能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「两个相互耦合的组件中该改哪一方」的评测设定，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据获取、latent 推理与停止决策之间的贡献分配问题类比，可供核查；但与视觉推理无直接联系。
